title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction: Section II sets up the problem of small transverse vibrations of a uniform elastic strip (lamina) AB. The strip is clamped at A into an immovable wall and free at B (a cantilever). It is bent into a nearly straight curve AYF. The abscissa x = BX is measured from the free end B, and the deflection is y = XY. Because y is treated as infinitesimal, arc lengths equal their projections: arc FY ≈ x and arc AY ≈ AX. With linear density K/k (mass K per length k), the following hold: (1) the mass of the portion FY is Kx/k; (2) the mass of an element is K dx/k; (3) the total mass is Ka/k, where a = BA. The radius of curvature, with dx taken as constant, is r = ds^3/(dx ddy). With ds ≈ dx this becomes r ≈ dx^2/ddy, i.e. curvature ≈ y''. Using the constitutive law from §I (bending moment = elastic constant · cc / r), the moment needed to hold this curvature at Y is Kcc·ddy/dx^2. Euler reads this as a static equivalence: a force Ff applied at the free end F would have to produce exactly this moment about Y. In modern terms, M(x) = EI·y''(x), the linearized Euler–Bernoulli bending relation. It is the first step toward the beam equation y_tt ∝ −c^2 y_xxxx, which is derived on the following pages via partial derivatives and d'Alembert-type accelerations.
errors: No mathematical errors. The approximations (arc = abscissa, ds = dx, and r = dx^2/ddy with sign set by the 'sursum vergentis' convention) are the standard small-deflection linearization. One notational point: the previous page's transcription gives the moment as Ecc/r, while this page (and the next) write Kcc. Either the earlier transcription is wrong or Euler absorbs the elastic constant into K·cc (cc being an elasticity parameter scaled by the weight K). This is a constant-convention issue, not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Linearized bending-moment–curvature relation M = (const)·y'' for small deflections of a uniform strip
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jacob Bernoulli (moment ∝ curvature), with Daniel Bernoulli and Euler (1730s–1740s)
ideas.where_published: Euler, Methodus inveniendi (1744), Additamentum I De curvis elasticis; earlier vibrating-lamina work (E40, De sono campanarum / lamina papers); Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (OO II.11.2)

ideas.what: Cantilever setup with abscissa from the free end and mass distribution K dx/k
ideas.where_published: Euler 1744 Additamentum; D. Bernoulli, Comm. Acad. Petrop. 13 (1741–43)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely routine setup page. It restates the standard linearized moment-curvature law for a cantilever strip, which Euler and Daniel Bernoulli had published decades earlier. The paper's novelties (new vibration modes and the PDE treatment) come later.
transcription_corrections: 'ex formulis notissimis ra.. i osculi' in the image (smudged) reads 'radii osculi', as the machine transcription correctly gives.
The moment is clearly printed 'Kcc ddy/dx^2' (with K, not E). The previous page's 'Ecc/r' should be checked against that image and may be an OCR error for 'Kcc/r'.
